name: score
title: Score
description: Safety-score figure in a semantic fill at three control densities and an optional dense value treatment.

intent.summary: Safety-score figure in a semantic fill at three control densities and an optional dense value treatment.
useWhen: A driver or fleet safety score needs its fair, good, or excellent fill and the numeric figure in one place.
The same score treatment appears in Card Overview, an in-card summary, or a compact row such as a table group header.
avoidWhen: The figure is an ordinary metric without a safety-score color band; use Text.
The score is one cell in a comparable measures grid that also needs period chrome; use CardOverview, which composes Score.
The mark is a notification count or status label; use Badge or Tag.
A comparison trend should sit beside the fill; keep trend in the owner. Card Overview already renders score trend in its copy column.

alternatives.when: The figure is one of several comparable measures under a shared period bar.
alternatives.reason: CardOverview owns the summary grid, period chrome, score-cell alignment, and score trend; it renders Score at lg with the dense figure treatment.

alternatives.when: The quantity is ordinary readable content without a safety-score fill.
alternatives.reason: Text preserves the figure as body content.

alternatives.when: The compact mark is unread count or notification presence.
alternatives.reason: Badge owns supplemental notification chrome, not a scored figure.

accessibility: Set label when the atomic score graphic needs a spoken prefix such as Safety score; the visible number remains in the fill.
Colour never carries score meaning alone; the numeric figure stays visible inside the fill.
Score is not interactive and is not a tab stop.
While loading, the host exposes a busy state and a skeleton whose type metrics match the resolved size and variant.
states: The default figure uses emphasized title typography: lg uses title-large, md uses title-medium, and sm uses title-small. Use the default treatment for standalone, table, and in-card scores.

The dense variant preserves the selected fill dimensions and uses a larger emphasized figure: lg uses display-small, md uses title-large, and sm uses title-medium. Use dense when a composition intentionally needs less space around the value; Card Overview owns this treatment for its headline score.
The fill dimensions remain 56 by 40 at lg, 40 by 32 at md, and 28 by 24 at sm. The fill box crops the type canvas so line-height does not change the declared size.

A numeric value from 0–100 infers fair from 0–50, good from 51–80, and excellent from 81–100. Empty or whitespace-only values stay on the faint neutral surface. Supply level explicitly when another displayed value needs a semantic fill.
The fill uses the safety-score background and keeps its foreground at AA text contrast in light and dark themes.

isLoading replaces the figure with a skeleton at the matching size and variant type metrics. The skeleton uses the faint context when no score level is known and the bold context when a known or explicitly supplied level keeps its semantic fill.
responsiveBehavior: The owner selects sm, md, or lg to match the local layout. Score does not change size at breakpoints.
Table group heroes and in-card summaries use the default figure treatment. Card Overview composes the dense lg treatment for its headline score.

isLoading.description: Replace the figure with a skeleton while data resolves.

label.description: Accessible name prefix, for example “Safety score”.

level.description:
Safety-score color level. Numeric values from 0–100 infer fair (0–50),
good (51–80), or excellent (81–100) when this is omitted.

size.description:
Visual density matching control height: `sm` 24px, `md` 32px, `lg` 40px.
`lg` is the Card Overview recipe.

variant.description:
Value typography recipe. `dense` keeps the selected size's fill dimensions
and uses a larger emphasized figure with tighter surrounding space.
